As for the intensity, it used to just be a nagging worry, but over the last two months, it has become a constant, overwhelming conviction that I can't shake.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the suspicion started about a year ago but intensified over the last two months, can you clarify if there was a sudden change or event that triggered this intensification, or was it a gradual process?\n\nPatient: It was definitely a gradual process rather than a single, sudden shift. The nagging suspicion just slowly grew into a firm belief I couldn't shake, especially as the stress from my new role built up over the year and I kept getting blamed for routing mistakes that weren't my fault.\n\nDoctor: Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed, alongside these beliefs about your coworkers?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love, like my choir, softball, and going to church. I just feel totally empty and don't have the energy to do anything, so after work I usually just lie on the couch in my uniform without showering or cooking. It feels like too much effort to even talk, so I barely answer my husband when he tries to speak to me.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy and feeling empty, can you tell me more about when you first noticed this loss of interest and how it has affected your daily life and relationships?\n\nPatient: This loss of interest has been building for about a year since I took on that lead role, and I eventually just dropped out of my choir, softball, and church because I stopped caring. Now, I just lie on the couch in my work uniform without showering or cooking, which has really frustrated my husband. I barely help with chores anymore and only give him one-word answers because it takes too much effort to engage.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling empty and losing interest in activities, can you tell me if there are any activities or things that still bring you some pleasure or joy, even if it's just a little?\n\nPatient: No, nothing really brings me joy or pleasure anymore. I've completely stopped caring about everything I used to love, like my choir, softball, and church. Most days I just lie on the couch because it takes too much effort to feel or do anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any thoughts of death, wishing you were dead, or suicidal thoughts since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, I have not had any thoughts of death, wishing to be dead, or wanting to hurt myself. I am just feeling extremely exhausted, overwhelmed, and stressed by everything that is happening around me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are moments, even briefly, where you feel a slight pleasure or happiness, or is it a complete absence of any positive feelings?\n\nPatient: It is a complete absence of positive feelings, and I don't experience even brief moments of happiness anymore. I just feel completely flat, empty, and indifferent, even when I think about things I used to love like choir or softball. It honestly feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief that your coworkers are plotting against you relates to your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities, or do these feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel like separate issues, but they both contribute to how completely exhausted I am. The plotting at work makes me feel constantly defensive, stressed, and angry because I'm always on guard. But the loss of interest in choir, softball, and church is different—it just feels like a complete lack of energy and an inability to care about anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: When you're thinking about your coworkers plotting against you, do you ever have moments where you doubt this belief, or does it feel absolutely true to you all the time?\n\nPatient: It feels absolutely true to me all the time now, and I don't have any doubt about it. It is incredibly frustrating when my boss and others try to blame it on \"computer glitches\" because I am completely certain my coworkers are doing this on purpose to sabotage me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly change your mind about your coworkers plotting against you, or do you feel that this belief is unshakeable?\n\nPatient: No, this belief is completely unshakeable because I can't ignore the clear evidence I see with my own eyes, like my route maps being altered and drivers holding different printouts. Calling it \"computer glitches\" is just a convenient cover-up, and it is incredibly frustrating that everyone else refuses to see what is right in front of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and functioning would change if you were somehow convinced that your coworkers were not plotting against you, would your loss of interest in activities and feelings of emptiness improve?\n\nPatient: Even if I were convinced the plotting wasn't happening, I don't think this emptiness and loss of interest would suddenly get better. This heavy feeling of not caring actually started building a year ago, long before the plotting became a constant reality these past couple of months. It feels like a deep, separate exhaustion where it's just too much effort to care about anything, regardless of the work situation.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your strong belief in the plot against you is what's causing your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or do you feel like these are two separate issues that happen to be occurring at the same time?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel like separate issues to me because of the timeline. The emptiness, exhaustion, and losing interest in things like softball and choir started almost a year ago when the work stress first began. The realization that my coworkers are actively plotting and changing my routes is much more recent, only taking over in the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the plotting against you by your coworkers is the main reason for your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or are these feelings present even when you're not thinking about the plot?\n\nPatient: The emptiness and lack of energy are constant and present all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about the plotting. This heavy feeling of not caring started building slowly over a year ago, whereas the plotting only became clear and overwhelming in the last couple of months. They really feel like two different things, with the apathy always being there as a constant weight."

I am just feeling extremely exhausted, overwhelmed, and stressed by everything that is happening around me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are moments, even briefly, where you feel a slight pleasure or happiness, or is it a complete absence of any positive feelings?\n\nPatient: It is a complete absence of positive feelings, and I don't experience even brief moments of happiness anymore. I just feel completely flat, empty, and indifferent, even when I think about things I used to love like choir or softball. It honestly feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief that your coworkers are plotting against you relates to your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities, or do these feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel like separate issues, but they both contribute to how completely exhausted I am. The plotting at work makes me feel constantly defensive, stressed, and angry because I'm always on guard. But the loss of interest in choir, softball, and church is different—it just feels like a complete lack of energy and an inability to care about anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: When you're thinking about your coworkers plotting against you, do you ever have moments where you doubt this belief, or does it feel absolutely true to you all the time?\n\nPatient: It feels absolutely true to me all the time now, and I don't have any doubt about it. It is incredibly frustrating when my boss and others try to blame it on \"computer glitches\" because I am completely certain my coworkers are doing this on purpose to sabotage me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly change your mind about your coworkers plotting against you, or do you feel that this belief is unshakeable?\n\nPatient: No, this belief is completely unshakeable because I can't ignore the clear evidence I see with my own eyes, like my route maps being altered and drivers holding different printouts. Calling it \"computer glitches\" is just a convenient cover-up, and it is incredibly frustrating that everyone else refuses to see what is right in front of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and functioning would change if you were somehow convinced that your coworkers were not plotting against you, would your loss of interest in activities and feelings of emptiness improve?\n\nPatient: Even if I were convinced the plotting wasn't happening, I don't think this emptiness and loss of interest would suddenly get better. This heavy feeling of not caring actually started building a year ago, long before the plotting became a constant reality these past couple of months. It feels like a deep, separate exhaustion where it's just too much effort to care about anything, regardless of the work situation.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your strong belief in the plot against you is what's causing your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or do you feel like these are two separate issues that happen to be occurring at the same time?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel like separate issues to me because of the timeline. The emptiness, exhaustion, and losing interest in things like softball and choir started almost a year ago when the work stress first began. The realization that my coworkers are actively plotting and changing my routes is much more recent, only taking over in the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the plotting against you by your coworkers is the main reason for your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or are these feelings present even when you're not thinking about the plot?\n\nPatient: The emptiness and lack of energy are constant and present all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about the plotting. This heavy feeling of not caring started building slowly over a year ago, whereas the plotting only became clear and overwhelming in the last couple of months. They really feel like two different things, with the apathy always being there as a constant weight.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your belief that coworkers are plotting against you affects your daily functioning and relationships, compared to the feelings of emptiness and loss of interest you've been experiencing?\n\nPatient: The plotting at work keeps me constantly tense and defensive, which has led to arguments with drivers and a formal write-up because I'm trying to protect myself from their sabotage. Meanwhile, the emptiness completely drains me at home, causing me to drop out of choir and softball and withdraw from my husband because I just don't have the energy to care or do anything.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if the plotting by your coworkers were to stop, your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities would also improve, or would they remain a problem for you?\n\nPatient: I think they would still be a problem, because my loss of interest and feeling drained started almost a year ago with the extra work responsibilities, whereas the plotting only became clear in the last couple of months. I feel so completely empty and lacking in energy that I don't think simply stopping the plotting would bring my motivation back. It just feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times or situations where your belief about the coworkers plotting against you might not be entirely accurate, or is it always consistent with what you observe and experience?\n\nPatient: It is completely consistent and feels entirely real to me, and I cannot shake this conviction at all. There are no times where it isn't accurate because the evidence of them altering my routes is right in front of me. My boss trying to blame it on \"computer glitches\" is just wrong, because I know they are deliberately sabotaging my work.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that coworkers are plotting against you is the primary cause of your current distress, or are your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities contributing more to your overall distress?\n\nPatient: Both are deeply distressing, but they affect me in different ways. The plotting at work causes intense anger and anxiety because it feels like an active threat to my job and my sanity, while losing my choir, softball, and church makes me feel completely hollow, like I am losing who I am. The plotting feels much more urgent and alarming, but the emptiness is a heavy, constant weight that I just can't shake off.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities would improve if your concerns about your coworkers plotting against you were addressed, or do you see these as entirely separate issues?"

It feels like a deep, separate exhaustion where it's just too much effort to care about anything, regardless of the work situation.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your strong belief in the plot against you is what's causing your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or do you feel like these are two separate issues that happen to be occurring at the same time?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel like separate issues to me because of the timeline. The emptiness, exhaustion, and losing interest in things like softball and choir started almost a year ago when the work stress first began. The realization that my coworkers are actively plotting and changing my routes is much more recent, only taking over in the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the plotting against you by your coworkers is the main reason for your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or are these feelings present even when you're not thinking about the plot?\n\nPatient: The emptiness and lack of energy are constant and present all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about the plotting. This heavy feeling of not caring started building slowly over a year ago, whereas the plotting only became clear and overwhelming in the last couple of months. They really feel like two different things, with the apathy always being there as a constant weight.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your belief that coworkers are plotting against you affects your daily functioning and relationships, compared to the feelings of emptiness and loss of interest you've been experiencing?\n\nPatient: The plotting at work keeps me constantly tense and defensive, which has led to arguments with drivers and a formal write-up because I'm trying to protect myself from their sabotage. The nagging suspicion just slowly grew into a firm belief I couldn't shake, especially as the stress from my new role built up over the year and I kept getting blamed for routing mistakes that weren't my fault.\n\nDoctor: Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed, alongside these beliefs about your coworkers?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love, like my choir, softball, and going to church. I just feel totally empty and don't have the energy to do anything, so after work I usually just lie on the couch in my uniform without showering or cooking. It feels like too much effort to even talk, so I barely answer my husband when he tries to speak to me.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy and feeling empty, can you tell me more about when you first noticed this loss of interest and how it has affected your daily life and relationships?\n\nPatient: This loss of interest has been building for about a year since I took on that lead role, and I eventually just dropped out of my choir, softball, and church because I stopped caring. Now, I just lie on the couch in my work uniform without showering or cooking, which has really frustrated my husband. I barely help with chores anymore and only give him one-word answers because it takes too much effort to engage.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling empty and losing interest in activities, can you tell me if there are any activities or things that still bring you some pleasure or joy, even if it's just a little?\n\nPatient: No, nothing really brings me joy or pleasure anymore. I've completely stopped caring about everything I used to love, like my choir, softball, and church. Most days I just lie on the couch because it takes too much effort to feel or do anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any thoughts of death, wishing you were dead, or suicidal thoughts since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, I have not had any thoughts of death, wishing to be dead, or wanting to hurt myself. I am just feeling extremely exhausted, overwhelmed, and stressed by everything that is happening around me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are moments, even briefly, where you feel a slight pleasure or happiness, or is it a complete absence of any positive feelings?\n\nPatient: It is a complete absence of positive feelings, and I don't experience even brief moments of happiness anymore. I just feel completely flat, empty, and indifferent, even when I think about things I used to love like choir or softball. It honestly feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief that your coworkers are plotting against you relates to your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities, or do these feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel like separate issues, but they both contribute to how completely exhausted I am. The plotting at work makes me feel constantly defensive, stressed, and angry because I'm always on guard. But the loss of interest in choir, softball, and church is different—it just feels like a complete lack of energy and an inability to care about anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: When you're thinking about your coworkers plotting against you, do you ever have moments where you doubt this belief, or does it feel absolutely true to you all the time?\n\nPatient: It feels absolutely true to me all the time now, and I don't have any doubt about it. It is incredibly frustrating when my boss and others try to blame it on \"computer glitches\" because I am completely certain my coworkers are doing this on purpose to sabotage me.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly change your mind about your coworkers plotting against you, or do you feel that this belief is unshakeable?\n\nPatient: No, this belief is completely unshakeable because I can't ignore the clear evidence I see with my own eyes, like my route maps being altered and drivers holding different printouts. Calling it \"computer glitches\" is just a convenient cover-up, and it is incredibly frustrating that everyone else refuses to see what is right in front of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and functioning would change if you were somehow convinced that your coworkers were not plotting against you, would your loss of interest in activities and feelings of emptiness improve?\n\nPatient: Even if I were convinced the plotting wasn't happening, I don't think this emptiness and loss of interest would suddenly get better. This heavy feeling of not caring actually started building a year ago, long before the plotting became a constant reality these past couple of months. It feels like a deep, separate exhaustion where it's just too much effort to care about anything, regardless of the work situation.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your strong belief in the plot against you is what's causing your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or do you feel like these are two separate issues that happen to be occurring at the same time?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel like separate issues to me because of the timeline. The emptiness, exhaustion, and losing interest in things like softball and choir started almost a year ago when the work stress first began. The realization that my coworkers are actively plotting and changing my routes is much more recent, only taking over in the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the plotting against you by your coworkers is the main reason for your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or are these feelings present even when you're not thinking about the plot?\n\nPatient: The emptiness and lack of energy are constant and present all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about the plotting. This heavy feeling of not caring started building slowly over a year ago, whereas the plotting only became clear and overwhelming in the last couple of months. They really feel like two different things, with the apathy always being there as a constant weight.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your belief that coworkers are plotting against you affects your daily functioning and relationships, compared to the feelings of emptiness and loss of interest you've been experiencing?\n\nPatient: The plotting at work keeps me constantly tense and defensive, which has led to arguments with drivers and a formal write-up because I'm trying to protect myself from their sabotage. Meanwhile, the emptiness completely drains me at home, causing me to drop out of choir and softball and withdraw from my husband because I just don't have the energy to care or do anything.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if the plotting by your coworkers were to stop, your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities would also improve, or would they remain a problem for you?\n\nPatient: I think they would still be a problem, because my loss of interest and feeling drained started almost a year ago with the extra work responsibilities, whereas the plotting only became clear in the last couple of months. I feel so completely empty and lacking in energy that I don't think simply stopping the plotting would bring my motivation back. It just feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times or situations where your belief about the coworkers plotting against you might not be entirely accurate, or is it always consistent with what you observe and experience?\n\nPatient: It is completely consistent and feels entirely real to me, and I cannot shake this conviction at all. There are no times where it isn't accurate because the evidence of them altering my routes is right in front of me. My boss trying to blame it on \"computer glitches\" is just wrong, because I know they are deliberately sabotaging my work.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that coworkers are plotting against you is the primary cause of your current distress, or are your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities contributing more to your overall distress?\n\nPatient: Both are deeply distressing, but they affect me in different ways. The plotting at work causes intense anger and anxiety because it feels like an active threat to my job and my sanity, while losing my choir, softball, and church makes me feel completely hollow, like I am losing who I am. The plotting feels much more urgent and alarming, but the emptiness is a heavy, constant weight that I just can't shake off.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities would improve if your concerns about your coworkers plotting against you were addressed, or do you see these as entirely separate issues?\n\nPatient: They feel like separate issues because the emptiness, exhaustion, and losing interest in choir and softball started much earlier in the year when I first got overwhelmed by my new role, whereas the plotting only became clear in the last couple of months. I feel so completely drained and empty now that I'm not sure if fixing the work situation would actually bring my energy or interest back. It just feels like too much effort to care either way.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there's any possibility that your feelings of being plotted against could be related to your overall mood and stress, rather than an actual plot by your coworkers?\n\nPatient: No, there is absolutely no way this is just stress or my mood. While it started as a nagging suspicion, it has now become something I absolutely cannot shake, and I am certain they are actively sabotaging me. It's incredibly frustrating because everyone acts like I'm just crazy or imagining things, but I know what they're doing.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about your coworkers plotting against you, and was there a specific event or time when these thoughts started?\n\nPatient: The intense feeling that they are actively plotting and changing my routes has really taken over in the last couple of months, though it started as a nagging suspicion before that. Looking back, the overall stress and feeling off started about a year ago when I was informally pushed into a demanding lead role at work.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'the overall stress and feeling off started about a year ago'? Was there a specific event or period when your perceptions of being plotted against began to shift from a nagging suspicion to a more intense belief?\n\nPatient: About a year ago, I was informally pushed into a lead role with a massive workload, which is when I first started feeling overwhelmed and slipping at my job. But it was just in the last two months, around the time I got a formal write-up for a routing mistake, that the suspicion turned into a firm conviction that they are actively changing my maps to ruin my career.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief in the plot against you has affected your daily life and interactions with others, and have you noticed any fluctuations in the intensity of these beliefs over time?\n\nPatient: It has completely ruined my life outside of work—I've stopped going to choir, softball, and church, and my husband is really frustrated with me because I barely talk to him or help around the house anymore. As for the intensity, it used to just be a nagging worry, but over the last two months, it has become a constant, overwhelming conviction that I can't shake.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned the suspicion started about a year ago but intensified over the last two months, can you clarify if there was a sudden change or event that triggered this intensification, or was it a gradual process?\n\nPatient: It was definitely a gradual process rather than a single, sudden shift. The nagging suspicion just slowly grew into a firm belief I couldn't shake, especially as the stress from my new role built up over the year and I kept getting blamed for routing mistakes that weren't my fault.\n\nDoctor: Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed, alongside these beliefs about your coworkers?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love, like my choir, softball, and going to church. I just feel totally empty and don't have the energy to do anything, so after work I usually just lie on the couch in my uniform without showering or cooking. It feels like too much effort to even talk, so I barely answer my husband when he tries to speak to me.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy and feeling empty, can you tell me more about when you first noticed this loss of interest and how it has affected your daily life and relationships?\n\nPatient: This loss of interest has been building for about a year since I took on that lead role, and I eventually just dropped out of my choir, softball, and church because I stopped caring. Now, I just lie on the couch in my work uniform without showering or cooking, which has really frustrated my husband. I barely help with chores anymore and only give him one-word answers because it takes too much effort to engage.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling empty and losing interest in activities, can you tell me if there are any activities or things that still bring you some pleasure or joy, even if it's just a little?\n\nPatient: No, nothing really brings me joy or pleasure anymore. I've completely stopped caring about everything I used to love, like my choir, softball, and church. Most days I just lie on the couch because it takes too much effort to feel or do anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any thoughts of death, wishing you were dead, or suicidal thoughts since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, I have not had any thoughts of death, wishing to be dead, or wanting to hurt myself. I am just feeling extremely exhausted, overwhelmed, and stressed by everything that is happening around me.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if there are moments, even briefly, where you feel a slight pleasure or happiness, or is it a complete absence of any positive feelings?\n\nPatient: It is a complete absence of positive feelings, and I don't experience even brief moments of happiness anymore. I just feel completely flat, empty, and indifferent, even when I think about things I used to love like choir or softball. It honestly feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your belief that your coworkers are plotting against you relates to your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities, or do these feel like separate issues to you?\n\nPatient: They feel like separate issues, but they both contribute to how completely exhausted I am. Calling it \"computer glitches\" is just a convenient cover-up, and it is incredibly frustrating that everyone else refuses to see what is right in front of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and functioning would change if you were somehow convinced that your coworkers were not plotting against you, would your loss of interest in activities and feelings of emptiness improve?\n\nPatient: Even if I were convinced the plotting wasn't happening, I don't think this emptiness and loss of interest would suddenly get better. This heavy feeling of not caring actually started building a year ago, long before the plotting became a constant reality these past couple of months. It feels like a deep, separate exhaustion where it's just too much effort to care about anything, regardless of the work situation.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your strong belief in the plot against you is what's causing your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or do you feel like these are two separate issues that happen to be occurring at the same time?\n\nPatient: They definitely feel like separate issues to me because of the timeline. The emptiness, exhaustion, and losing interest in things like softball and choir started almost a year ago when the work stress first began. The realization that my coworkers are actively plotting and changing my routes is much more recent, only taking over in the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the plotting against you by your coworkers is the main reason for your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest, or are these feelings present even when you're not thinking about the plot?\n\nPatient: The emptiness and lack of energy are constant and present all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about the plotting. This heavy feeling of not caring started building slowly over a year ago, whereas the plotting only became clear and overwhelming in the last couple of months. They really feel like two different things, with the apathy always being there as a constant weight.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how your belief that coworkers are plotting against you affects your daily functioning and relationships, compared to the feelings of emptiness and loss of interest you've been experiencing?\n\nPatient: The plotting at work keeps me constantly tense and defensive, which has led to arguments with drivers and a formal write-up because I'm trying to protect myself from their sabotage. Meanwhile, the emptiness completely drains me at home, causing me to drop out of choir and softball and withdraw from my husband because I just don't have the energy to care or do anything.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if the plotting by your coworkers were to stop, your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities would also improve, or would they remain a problem for you?\n\nPatient: I think they would still be a problem, because my loss of interest and feeling drained started almost a year ago with the extra work responsibilities, whereas the plotting only became clear in the last couple of months. I feel so completely empty and lacking in energy that I don't think simply stopping the plotting would bring my motivation back. It just feels like too much effort to feel anything at all.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times or situations where your belief about the coworkers plotting against you might not be entirely accurate, or is it always consistent with what you observe and experience?\n\nPatient: It is completely consistent and feels entirely real to me, and I cannot shake this conviction at all. There are no times where it isn't accurate because the evidence of them altering my routes is right in front of me. My boss trying to blame it on \"computer glitches\" is just wrong, because I know they are deliberately sabotaging my work.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your belief that coworkers are plotting against you is the primary cause of your current distress, or are your feelings of emptiness and loss of interest in activities contributing more to your overall distress?\n\nPatient: Both are deeply distressing, but they affect me in different ways.
